//: Migrations run before the server starts, and the '&&' matters: if a
migration fails the process never serves. Starting anyway would mean
answering requests against a schema the code does not expect, which is
how you corrupt data rather than merely have an outage.
Safe to run on every boot because migrations are idempotent and guarded
by the schema_migrations ledger. With several instances they could race,
but each runs in a transaction and records itself, so the loser is a
no-op. Revisit if this ever scales past one instance.
